nodes.name: Mo powder oxidation
nodes.procedure: 0.4 g of Mo powder was dispersed in 40 mL of ethanol with magnetic stirring for 10 min. Then, 1.2 mL of H2O2 (30%) solution was injected dropwise into the suspension. After stirring for 12 h at room temperature, the solution turned into a dark blue color.
nodes.source_text: 0.4g of Mo powder was dispersed in 40 mL of ethanol... the solution turned into a dark blue color.

nodes.name: precursor solution formation
nodes.procedure: Separately, 10 mg of Ni(OCOCH3)2·4H2O was dissolved in 10 mL of ethanol and mixed with the dark blue suspension to form the precursor solution.
nodes.source_text: Separately, 10mg of Ni(OCOCH_3)_2·4H_2O was dissolved in 10mL of ethanol and mixed with the dark blue suspension to form the precursor.

nodes.name: Ni-induced salt-templated synthesis
nodes.procedure: The precursor solution was then mixed with 640 g of NaCl powder and dried at 50°C with continuous hand stirring. After that, the mixture was annealed at 750°C for 5 h at a heating rate of 1°C min⁻¹ under a 5% NH3/Ar atmosphere. Finally, the product was washed with deionized water and dilute hydrochloric acid several times to remove the NaCl template and Ni nanoparticles before being dried using vacuum filtration.

nodes.name: MoN salt-templated synthesis
nodes.procedure: The 2D MoN nanosheets were synthesized without the addition of Ni. The Mo precursor was mixed with 640g of NaCl and annealed at 750°C for 5h. The final product was obtained by removing NaCl using deionized water and vacuum filtration.
nodes.source_text: The 2D MoN nanosheets were synthesized without the addition of Ni. The Mo precursor was mixed with 640g of NaCl and annealed at 750°C for 5h...

nodes.name: Ni0.2Mo0.8N synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.26 g of Ni(OCOCH3)2·4H2O was added into the Mo precursor and directly annealed the mixture without the salt-template at 550°C at a heating rate of 3°C min⁻¹ for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: Ni_{0.2}Mo_{0.8}N was synthesized by adding 0.26g of Ni(OCOCH_3)_2·4H_2O into the Mo precursor...

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 630 mg of hexamethylenetetramine was dissolved in 100 mL of deionized water and purged with N2 gas. Then, 120 mg of NiCl2·6H2O was added to the solution. The reactants were heated under reflux temperature for 12 h with continuous N2 flow. Light green products were collected from the flask, washed with water and ethanol several times, and freeze-dried for the following steps.
nodes.source_text: 630 mg of hexamethylenetetramine was dissolved in 100 mL... freeze-dried for the following steps.

nodes.name: Ni3N synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)2 was then prepared by annealing Ni(OH)2 at 390°C for 2 h at a heating rate of 3°C min⁻¹ under a 5% NH3/Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Ni_3N was then prepared by annealing Ni(OH)_2 at 390°C for 2 h...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Mo5N6 show different peak positions compared to MoN, indicating extra 20% nitrogen incorporation changes the crystal structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through a comparison of the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns, the synthesized Mo5N6 possesses the different peak position with that of MoN (Figure 2a), indicating that the extra (20%) nitrogen-incorporation can greatly change the crystal structure of conventional MoN.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM imaging shows 2D morphology of Mo5N6 nanosheets that are transparent and wrinkled.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 2D morphology of the Mo5N6 nanosheets were observed under scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging, which showed that the nanosheets are transparent and wrinkled (Figure 2b, Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Mo5N6 nanosheet is 3 nm thick with uniformly exposed lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the Mo5N6 nanosheet is only 3 nm thick, demonstrating its atomically thin 2D structure with uniformly exposed lattice and large surface area (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Mo 3d XPS spectra show dominant Mo 4+ valence state (binding energy 230.0 eV) in Mo5N6 vs Mo 3+ (229.3 eV) in MoN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the high-resolution Mo 3d XPS spectra (Figure 3a), the dominant valence state of Mo in Mo5N6 is 4+ (binding energy of 230.0 eV), which is higher than that of MoN (+3, binding energy of 229.3 eV).

nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo LIII-edge XANES spectrum also confirms the higher oxidation state of the Mo cation in Mo5N6 than that of MoN (Figure 3b), by identifying a positive energy shift of 0.5 eV... As shown in Figure 3c, the relative peak intensity of Mo5N6 at 399.0 eV is stronger than the peak at 401.3 eV, indicating that more N 1s electrons transfer to the p-d(t2g) orbital compared to in MoN...

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo5N6 shows smaller electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl than MoN, indicating enhanced performance derives from optimized adsorption energy not surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Importantly, Mo5N6 shows a smaller electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) than MoN, indicating that the enhanced performance of Mo5N6 does not derive from the surface area but from the optimized adsorption energy of key intermediates on the surface (Figures S9 and S10).
